description: Canonical orchestration method: capability vocabulary, cost tiers, effort levels, role aliases, and the three routing rules. Read by both the Python engine (orchestrator/method.py) and the HT bridge (bridge/extensions/orchestrator/models.ts via a symlink). Editing this file edits the method; SKILL.md summarises it for humans and must not contradict it. Runtime config (pricing, features, persistence) stays in config.json; per-dispatch spend caps are method policy (rules.dispatch_spend_cap); runtime state (history, measured ROI) stays in ~/.local/state/coding-agent-orchestrator/.

review_after_fix.summary: Re-review after a fix uses at least the original reviewer's tier; never the cheap tier.
review_after_fix.rationale: After a fix, the code under review has changed. The cheap tier confirmed 4/4 re-reviews in early data, but downstream tasks proceeded without issue only because the fixes were small. A single regression missed by a cheap re-reviewer costs more in rework and escaped defects than the entire cheap re-review savings to date ($0.31).

pre_implementation_recon.summary: Tasks at complexity >= 5 get a parallel fan-out of cheap, read-only recon workers before any implementer touches code. The orchestrator extension owns this fan-out directly (it is a billed, observable dispatch); leads must not re-run their own recon.
pre_implementation_recon.rationale: implementation_strong-class tasks with 150K-400K input tokens cost $0.55-$2.38 because the implementer reads raw repository context. Cheap scouts pre-digesting that context into one bounded evidence packet save $1+ on the most expensive implementer calls and improve focus.
pre_implementation_recon.evidence_packet_rationale: evidence_packet_max_tokens is the AGGREGATE budget for the single combined packet handed to each lead, not a per-scout allowance: the cost being bounded is the lead's input prompt, which carries every scout's output at once. Each of the N workers therefore gets an equal share (budget / N), and the combined packet is capped at the total again after assembly. Failed workers are allocated their header plus a fair share of diagnostic space before any successful output, so a failure can never be hidden by a verbose success.

exploration_topology.summary: Investigation, recon and digest work uses the cheapest sufficient capability: one capable lead plus 3-5 parallel cheap workers.
exploration_topology.rationale: The ht-codex-modularization-status run proved this topology: 4 parallel mid-tier scouts produced complete evidence packets at near-zero cost, and a single premium synthesis produced the status report. Sending the premium model to do the investigation itself would have cost 5-10x more.

lead_sizing.summary: Triage picks a lead size; profiles bind sizes to models through tiers.
lead_sizing.rationale: 2026-09-24: fable-5-1 leads cost $90.71 over 17 runs (11 verified pass); sonnet-5 leads cost $1.04 over 21 runs (19 verified pass). Size the lead to the task and escalate on failure instead of pinning the frontier model.

dispatch_spend_cap.summary: Per-dispatch USD ceiling on live reported cost. warn notifies once; enforce also cancels the dispatch; off disables.

efficiency_controls.summary: Phase-2 opt-in efficiency switches. Every switch defaults OFF; each is independent. Off = byte-identical baseline behaviour.

model_canaries.summary: Comparison candidates only; never primary replacements or automatic promotions. 0% exposure until explicitly enabled AND qualification is available.
model_canaries.activation_unavailable_reason: catalog model qualification (tool/context/reasoning requirement checks) is not on main; it exists only on the unmerged feat/model-failover branch
